definition: A retrieval-augmented generation variant that builds and queries a knowledge graph extracted from source documents, rather than retrieving flat text chunks.
details: GraphRAG aims to improve on standard RAG for tasks requiring understanding of relationships and structure across a corpus (such as summarizing themes across many documents), by first organizing extracted entities and relations into a graph.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Here is the short version: A retrieval-augmented generation variant that builds and queries a knowledge graph extracted from source documents, rather than retrieving flat text chunks. The part that makes it sing: GraphRAG aims to improve on standard RAG for tasks requiring understanding of relationships and structure across a corpus (such as summarizing themes across many documents), by first organizing extracted entities and relations into a graph. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — GraphRAG — is what makes everything else possible.

citation.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
